title: In the federal record, "more crops" means more insecticide, not less
subtitle: County crop diversity vs. insecticide applied per harvested acre. The rising national line is crop identity, not landscape structure: among counties that grow no cotton, vegetable, orchard, berry, rice, peanut, tobacco, sugar or hop acreage, the gradient disappears.

x.label: Effective number of crops in the county (exp of Shannon entropy over harvested acres)
x.note: Rows are binned on effective_n_crops; enc_bin gives the bin edges and enc_median the within-bin median. Bins are shared across series so the three lines are directly comparable.

y.label: Insecticide + acaricide applied, grams per acre of harvested cropland (median county)
y.note: Log scale because the national series spans 7.7 to 116 g/acre. The p25-p75 band should be drawn for 'All counties' and 'No high-input crop grown'; drawing all three bands is too busy.

annotations.text: 116 g/acre. Median 28% of harvested cropland in a high-input crop.
7.7 g/acre. 270 of these 284 'simplest' counties are hay-dominated rangeland, not industrial monoculture.
Flat. Once crop identity is held out, county crop diversity carries no information about insecticide intensity.

USGS builds each county pesticide estimate by multiplying Census of Agriculture county harvested acreage of each crop by a Crop Reporting District median pesticide-by-crop application rate (Thelin & Stone 2013, USGS SIR 2013-5009). The x and y axes are therefore partly the same measurement. Neither axis contains any information about field size, edge density, patch configuration or seminatural habitat.

source_note: USDA NASS Census of Agriculture 2017 (Quick Stats bulk, county level) and USGS Pesticide National Synthesis Project EPest-high county estimates for 2018, corrected basis (California excluded in every year, aggregate rows removed). 2,416 counties, 303.5 million harvested acres = 97.2% of non-California US harvested cropland. Insecticide = a 70-compound roster of conventional synthetic insecticides, acaricides and insect-active nematicides; soil fumigants, oils, sulfur and microbials excluded. Computed by analysis/kremen/compute.py.
